title: Open the manual page for a command
summary: Every standard command has a manual page that explains what it does and lists its options. You open it in the terminal, scroll and search inside it, and close it when you are done.
prerequisites: Know the name of the command you want to read about, for example ls
The manual pages are installed; on minimal Linux systems or containers install the man-db and man-pages packages (Fedora also needs util-linux)

steps.explain: Check that a manual page exists for the command. This only prints the file path of the page and does not open it.

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: Name of the command you want to read about

steps.expect: A file path such as /usr/share/man/man1/ls.1.gz on Linux or /usr/share/man/man1/ls.1 on macOS. 'No manual entry' means there is no page under that name.

steps.explain: Open the manual page. It fills the window and the top line shows the command name and the section number in parentheses, for example LS(1); section 1 holds user commands.

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: Name of the command you want to read about

steps.expect: Headings such as NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION and OPTIONS. The page is shown in a pager, so you can scroll it.

alternatives.explain: Open the page from one specific manual section. Use it when a name has pages in several sections, for example printf is both a command and a C library function.

placeholders.name: SECTION
placeholders.description: Manual section number: 1 for user commands, 5 for file formats, 8 for admin commands

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: Name of the command you want to read about

alternatives.expect: The same page layout, taken only from the chosen section.

steps.explain: Read and search inside the page. Space or PageDown scrolls down, b or PageUp scrolls up, and the arrow keys move one line. Type / and a word then Enter to search, and n jumps to the next match.
Close the manual and return to the shell prompt by pressing q.

verify.expect: Prints the file path of the ls manual page and returns to the prompt.
